title: Hybrid Intelligence Research at the University of Oulu — Position Paper 2025
summary: Position paper formalising HI as co-evolution paradigm; four research themes include "Understanding humans in AI interaction." Anchors Oulu's 2023–2028 flagship. Directly feeds HASRL + MAI research streams.

title: Human and artificial intelligence collaboration for socially shared regulation in learning (Järvelä, Nguyen, Hadwin, 2023, BJET)
summary: Introduces HASRL model + "trigger" concept. The seminal citation for hybrid human-AI regulation of learning — explicitly cited as foundation of MAI agent design.

title: Deliberative Interactions for Socially Shared Regulation in Collaborative Learning: An AI-Driven Learning Analytics Study (Dang, Nguyen, Järvelä, 2024, JLA 11(3))
summary: Three-layer human-AI collaborative analysis on 2,125 utterances → identifies Plan-and-Implementation (adaptive) vs Trials-and-Failure (maladaptive) deliberation patterns. Empirical proof point that LA+AI can detect regulatory failure.

title: MAI: Supporting Regulation of Learning with a Proactive AI Agent in Collaborative Learning Contexts (Edwards et al., 2025)
summary: System paper for MAI itself. Proactive agent recognises trigger contexts and prompts metacognitive awareness — agent does not regulate for the group, but raises awareness so they self-regulate. Direct implementation of HASRL.

title: Simulating Classroom Education with LLM-Empowered Agents (SimClass) (Zhang et al., NAACL 2025)
summary: Multi-agent classroom: teacher / classmate / manager / assistant agents. Demonstrates emergent group behaviours and Flanders Interaction Analysis fit. Tsinghua MAIC, but matches "AI classroom system" keyword directly.

title: Agentic Orchestration for Adaptive Educational Recommendations (Chaturvedi & Gunawardena, WSDM 2026)
summary: 18+ coordinated agents in 4-tier hierarchy (perception / domain / coordination / strategy). Deployed on 6,000-user platform. Closest published blueprint to a "multi-agent classroom OS."

title: AI Agent for Education: Von Neumann Multi-Agent System Framework (Jiang et al., GCCCE 2024)
summary: Architectural framework decomposing each education agent into control / logic / storage / I/O units; distinguishes outer human-knowledge circulation vs inner agent-swarm intelligence circulation.

title: Leveraging a Multi-Agent LLM-Based System to Educate Teachers in Hate Incidents Management (ARISE) (Gajewska et al., 2025)
summary: Multi-agent system for teacher training: persona-modelled students, retrieval-augmented prompting. Application example of multi-agent architecture for teacher PD rather than K-12 student learning.

title: Multi-Agent Design: Optimizing Agents with Better Prompts and Topologies (MASS) (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2502.02533)
summary: Three-stage prompt+topology optimisation. Key finding: "optimise individual agents before composition"; an optimised single agent with Self-Consistency beats a 9-agent SC with default prompts. Direct evidence that naive agent-counting hurts.

title: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation
summary: AutoGen is an open-source framework that allows developers to build LLM applications via multiple agents that can converse with each other to accomplish tasks. AutoGen agents are customizable, conversable, and can operate in various modes that employ combinations of LLMs, human inputs, and tools. Using AutoGen, developers can also flexibly define agent interaction behaviors. Both natural language and computer code can be used to program flexible conversation patterns for different applications. title: Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems
summary: Agents, language model-based systems capable of reasoning, planning, and acting are widely adopted in real-world tasks, yet how their performance changes as these systems scale across key dimensions remains underexplored. We introduce quantitative scaling principles for agent systems as a predictive model, capturing how performance varies with coordination, model capability, and measurable system and task factors. title: MIRACLE_Multi-Agent Intelligent Regulation to Advance Collaborative Learning Environment
summary: Effective collaboration requires Socially Shared Regulation (SSRL), but students often lack these skills. This study introduces the MIRACLE (Multi-Agent Intelligent Regulation to Advance Collaborative Learning Environment) system, which supports SSRL by orchestrating metacognitive regulation and proactively providing emotional and motivational support. We conducted a quasi-experimental study with 90 fifth-grade students. The experimental group (n=42) used a collaborative platform CocoNote equipped with MIRACLE, while the control group (n=48) used the same platform with a general GPT assistant.

title: Primer: An AI Framework for Instructor-Centered Educational Simulation Creation
summary: Educational simulations are a well-established pedagogical technique that gives learners opportunities to apply knowledge, respond to challenges, and reflect on their performance. High-quality simulations, however, are difficult to build, requiring instructor input, scenario design, character development, scaffolding, technical implementation, and repeated revision. summary: Large language models support personalized tutoring, content generation, and adaptive learning paths. However, capability development requires these resources and interactions to form a coherent learning process that evolves with the learner. A central challenge is to align goals, activities, and assessment while using learning evidence to decide what should follow. title: ProofPaths: An AI Agent Framework for Assessing Student Reasoning
summary: Students can use large language models to complete assignments, but a correct solution does not establish whether they understand the reasoning behind it. Individualized interviews can probe that understanding but require recurring staff effort. summary: As agentic AI in education shifts from reactive tools toward partners that take initiative and persist over time, a central question is how learners relate to, evaluate, and benefit from artificial agency. We conducted a longitudinal experiment in an undergraduate learning analytics course, in which 17 student teams (N = 48) collaborated with a persistent LLM-based teammate across weekly sessions. summary: In K-12 mathematics tutoring, student-tutor dialogue provides rich evidence of learners' problem-solving processes and sources of difficulty. Learning analytics research increasingly relies on large language models (LLMs) to extract such information from dialogue for a variety of downstream tasks, including knowledge tracing, behavioral modeling, and diagnosis of student reasoning errors. title: AICoFe Demo: AI-based Collaborative Feedback System
summary: Peer feedback promotes active learning, critical reflection, and skill development, but its effectiveness is often limited by the quality of feedback students provide. Recent advances in LLMs offer new opportunities to support peer feedback by generating more coherent and actionable feedback while preserving human oversight. This paper presents AICoFe, an AI-based collaborative feedback system designed to support teacher, peer, and self-assessment in higher education. summary: We present an AI-based web-oriented tool designed to support formative feedback for oral presentation slides in higher education: AISSA. It allows students to upload their slides before presentation and automatically receive rubric-based quantitative scores and qualitative feedback generated by large language models (LLMs). summary: When a student is stuck, a tutor faces the assistance dilemma: help given too early can hinder productive struggle, while help withheld too long leaves the student in a frustrating, persistent impasse (i.e., wheel spinning). Automated draft-comparison methods often produce granular edit operations that can fragment a single purposeful revision into multiple analytic units. summary: Generative artificial intelligence can turn learning analytics into personalized support, but feedback systems must decide when to intervene, which evidence to use, and how much assistance to provide. summary: Medical history taking is a dialogue-based clinical reasoning task in which learners must gather, organise, and integrate patient information while the consultation unfolds.
